headline_marked: OnePlus exits [[US and Europe markets]] amid Oppo restructuring
headline: OnePlus exits US and Europe markets amid Oppo restructuring
summary: OnePlus stops new product launches in Europe and North America. The company will still support existing users.
details: OnePlus has announced that it will no longer launch new products in Europe and North America. The company will continue to support existing users with after-sales support and software updates.

The decision is part of a corporate restructuring at parent company Oppo, which has faced declining smartphone shipments. OnePlus was founded in 2013 to make affordable Android phones for tech enthusiasts.
The company will continue to operate in China and sell Realme phones in other regions. OnePlus co-founder Carl Pei left the company in 2020 to start Nothing.
Smartphone shipments are predicted to decline by over 13% in 2026 due to limited memory chip supply. Oppo faced a double-digit shipment decline year-over-year in Q2 2026.
caption:
OnePlus exits US and Europe markets. What's behind the move?

OnePlus has announced that it will no longer launch new products in Europe and North America. The company will continue to support existing users with after-sales support and software updates.

The decision is part of a corporate restructuring at parent company Oppo, which has faced declining smartphone shipments. OnePlus was founded in 2013 to make affordable Android phones for tech enthusiasts.

The company will continue to operate in China and sell Realme phones in other regions. OnePlus co-founder Carl Pei left the company in 2020 to start Nothing.

Smartphone shipments are predicted to decline by over 13% in 2026 due to limited memory chip supply. Oppo faced a double-digit shipment decline year-over-year in Q2 2026.
